result: Multiple SLC4A family members (SLC4A4, SLC4A5, SLC4A7, SLC4A8) are expressed in primary human airway epithelial cells, with SLC4A4 being the most highly expressed, followed by SLC4A7, SLC4A8, and SLC4A5. Bestrophins are also expressed but at lower levels.
evaluation: Reviewers raised concerns about the characterization of SLC4A expression. Reviewer #1 and #2 questioned whether the arguments to exclude SLC4A5 and SLC4A8 as candidate HCO3- importers were sufficient, noting that 'the fact that transepithelial HCO3- transport generates a Isc does not prove that the importer is electrogenic' and that localization in other tissues doesn't rule out different localization in airways. Reviewers also questioned how relative mRNA abundance was determined and whether bands were confirmed by digestion. The request for information about Bestrophin expression was addressed in the data but reviewers sought clarification on their potential contribution.

result: S0859 inhibits basal bicarbonate secretion in primary human airway epithelial cells in a bicarbonate-dependent manner, indicating the presence of an electrogenic bicarbonate transporter at the basolateral membrane consistent with SLC4A4.
evaluation: Reviewers expressed concerns about the magnitude and interpretation of these findings. Reviewer #2 noted that 'the size of the S0859-inhibitable Isc (representing a HCO3- secretory current) in the hAECs is very small (~1 uAmp/cm2) in comparison with anion current measurements in similar cell models reported previously (~20 uAmp/cm2).' Reviewers requested additional experiments including effects of Cl- inclusion and forskolin stimulation to better judge the quality of the monolayers and the specificity of the findings. Reviewer #3 questioned whether S0859 is selective for SLC4A4 or might block other SLC4A family members.

result: Intracellular pH recovery from CO2-induced acidification in human airway epithelial cells depends on basolateral bicarbonate and sodium, and is blocked by S0859, demonstrating SLC4A4-dependent bicarbonate uptake.
evaluation: Reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these intracellular pH recovery experiments. The data showing Na+-dependent, bicarbonate-dependent, and S0859-sensitive pH recovery was accepted as evidence for SLC4A4 function. However, Reviewer #3 asked about the difference in timescale between intracellular acidification effects (Figure 1) versus ASL pH effects (Figure 2), suggesting some need for clarification but not fundamental disagreement with the findings.

result: SLC4A4 inhibition by S0859 decreases ASL pH under both resting and forskolin-stimulated conditions in human airway epithelial cell cultures, demonstrating a central role for SLC4A4 in ASL pH homeostasis.
evaluation: Reviewers requested clarification about these ASL pH measurements. Reviewer #3 asked for 'a statement about the time point at which the pH was considered to have settled' and commented on 'the difference in timescale between the effects on intracellular acidification (Figure 1) vs the effect on ASL pH which seems to take ~2hrs (Figure 2).' Reviewer #1 found the significance values in Figure 2B, D, F 'confusing' and requested clarification about what the symbols represent and how significance was calculated. These methodological concerns suggest uncertainty about the interpretation rather than outright rejection.

result: SLC4A4 is localized to the basolateral membrane and preferentially expressed in ciliated cells in human airways, as demonstrated by immunolocalization with acetylated tubulin.
evaluation: Reviewers raised significant questions about the cellular localization findings. Reviewer #2 noted that 'it is unclear how many other cell types (CC10-positive Club cells; ionocytes; goblet cells) are retrieved in these human airway cell cultures' and pointed out that in mouse studies and other human studies, 'CFTR (and pendrin) are expressed mainly in CC10+-secretory (Club) cells, not in ciliated cells. This raises the question whether SLC4A4 is also expressed in human Club cells and whether Club cells rather than ciliated cells are the major sources of HCO3- secreted into the ASL.' Reviewer #2 requested immunostaining of SLC4A4 in CC10+ cells to address this uncertainty.

result: In mouse trachea, UTP-induced (but not cAMP-induced) anion secretion has a significant bicarbonate component that is reduced by S0859, and basal bicarbonate secretion is also S0859-sensitive, indicating SLC4A4-dependent bicarbonate transport.
evaluation: Reviewers raised multiple concerns about the mouse trachea experiments. Reviewer #2 asked 'why the IBMX/forskolin/cAMP-induced anion current, in contrast to the UTP/ca2+-induced current, is not reduced in bicarbonate-free buffer' and noted that 'in mouse trachea, most if not all Fsk/cAMP-induced anion secretory current is CaCC-mediated, so there is a priori no reason why forskolin-induced currents would not be reduced (at least in part) in a HCO3- free buffer.' Reviewer #2 also questioned how S0859 can inhibit a 'basal' HCO3- secretory current after AO1 blocks CaCCs, asking 'Does HCO3- exit the cell at the apical side through tonically active CFTR, or through an electrogenic HCO3-/Cl- exchanger?' The transient negative Isc changes induced by S0859 also remained unexplained.

result: UTP induces intracellular acidification in mouse airway cells that is bicarbonate-dependent and reduced by S0859, indicating that both basal and UTP-induced bicarbonate secretion depend on SLC4A4 activity.
evaluation: Reviewer #3 noted that 'some effects are not fully reversible (Figure S3G)' and asked the authors to comment on this. This observation raises questions about the completeness of the S0859 effect and whether the partial reversibility indicates off-target effects or incomplete inhibition. The incomplete reversibility suggests some uncertainty about the specificity and interpretation of these findings.

result: Slc4a4-/- mice exhibit tracheal cartilage defects, loss of SLC4A4 expression in airways, preferential expression in Club cells (not ciliated cells) in wild-type mice, mucus accumulation throughout the airways, epithelial damage, and decreased transepithelial resistance.
evaluation: Reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these histological and anatomical observations in the Slc4a4-/- mice. The phenotypic characterization including mucus accumulation, epithelial damage, and the differential cellular localization in mouse (Club cells) versus human (ciliated cells) airways was accepted. The observation that mouse SLC4A4 localizes differently than in human was noted by reviewers in the context of discussing species differences but not challenged as incorrect.

result: Slc4a4-/- mouse airway cells show reduced UTP-induced intracellular acidification compared to wild-type, and lack sustained acidification after UTP washout, indicating that bicarbonate accumulates in airway cells via SLC4A4 and supports sustained secretion.
evaluation: Reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these intracellular pH measurements in the knockout mice. The reduced acidification in Slc4a4-/- cells and the differential response after UTP washout were accepted as evidence for SLC4A4-dependent bicarbonate accumulation and secretion.

result: Mucociliary clearance is significantly reduced in Slc4a4-/- mouse trachea compared to wild-type, with similar reductions observed in wild-type tissues bathed in HEPES buffer, demonstrating that bicarbonate transport via SLC4A4 is necessary for normal mucociliary clearance.
evaluation: Reviewers did not raise specific concerns about the mucociliary clearance measurements. The reduced clearance in Slc4a4-/- mice and the similar effect of removing bicarbonate from wild-type tissues were accepted as evidence linking SLC4A4 function to mucociliary clearance. However, Reviewer #3 noted that 'direct measurements of ASL volume and pH in the knockout mice would clearly strengthen part of the central thesis, although these measurements are admittedly difficult to perform,' indicating that additional supporting data would be valuable but acknowledging the technical challenges.

result: Slc4a4-null mice exhibit a CF-like lung phenotype characterized by mucus accumulation and reduced mucociliary clearance even when chloride secretion remains intact, demonstrating that SLC4A4 plays an important role in bicarbonate secretion and airway function.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the phenotypic observations but raised concerns about interpretation and confounding factors. Reviewer #2 noted that 'the systemic Slc4a4 null-mouse model used in this study is known to suffer from many abnormalities, including severe metabolic acidosis due to pRTA' and asked 'whether the reduced level of plasma HCO3- contributes to the lack of HCO3- secretion and reduced ASL pH in the trachea of the Slc4a4-/- mouse depends on the affinity of the NBCe1 transporter for HCO3- ions.' Reviewer #2 requested information about whether the transporter is saturated at 5 mM HCO3- or needs higher levels. Reviewer #3 questioned whether Isc measurements represent true 'resting conditions' since 'the ASL is essentially flooded and the ionic composition on the apical side is not likely to match that of a normal ASL.'

result: Bicarbonate secretion in mouse airways is mostly Ca2+-activated rather than cAMP-activated, contrasting with human airways, but both species share a basal bicarbonate secretory component dependent on SLC4A4.
evaluation: This conclusion was questioned by reviewers. Reviewer #2 asked 'why the IBMX/forskolin/cAMP-induced anion current, in contrast to the UTP/ca2+-induced current, is not reduced in bicarbonate-free buffer' and noted that 'in mouse trachea, most if not all Fsk/cAMP-induced anion secretory current is CaCC-mediated, so there is a priori no reason why forskolin-induced currents would not be reduced (at least in part) in a HCO3- free buffer.' This suggests the interpretation about the lack of cAMP-stimulated bicarbonate secretion may need reconsideration.

result: SLC4A4 localization differs between mouse and human airways, with mouse SLC4A4 expressed in CCSP+ Club cells rather than ciliated cells, consistent with the localization of CFTR, TMEM16A, and Pendrin in non-ciliated secretory cells, suggesting functional coupling occurs in Club cells in mouse.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this species difference in cellular localization. The observation that mouse SLC4A4 is in Club cells while human SLC4A4 is in ciliated cells was noted in the context of known species differences in airway ion transport. Reviewer #2 suggested that 'a comparison of Club cell-specific vs. ciliated cell-specific Slc4a4-/- mouse models would be useful to study the functional importance of SLC4A4 in each cell type in vivo,' indicating acceptance of the localization findings while suggesting future experiments.

result: Slc4a4-/- mice suffer from severe metabolic acidosis with decreased plasma bicarbonate (5.3 mM), but this reduced bicarbonate availability is unlikely to have influenced mucus accumulation in the airways because the transporter is fully saturated at 3 mM bicarbonate.
evaluation: Reviewers specifically questioned this interpretation. Reviewer #2 stated 'whether the reduced level of plasma HCO3- contributes to the lack of HCO3- secretion and reduced ASL pH in the trachea of the Slc4a4-/- mouse depends on the affinity of the NBCe1 transporter for HCO3- ions. Therefore it is of interest to learn whether the transporter is already saturated at 5 mM HCO3-, or needs higher serosal HCO3- levels, e.g. 24 mM. This could be addressed experimentally or at least discussed.' The authors' claim that saturation occurs at 3 mM was based on a previous citation, but reviewers wanted this verified in the context of the current study.

result: Lack of bicarbonate is pathologically more relevant than chloride secretion in mouse airways, as evidenced by the muco-obstructive phenotype in Slc4a4-/- mice but not in Slc12a2-/- mice (which lack the chloride importer NKCC1).
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge this comparative interpretation. The contrast between the phenotypes of Slc4a4-/- mice (which show mucus accumulation) and Slc12a2-/- mice (which do not) was accepted as evidence that bicarbonate transport is more critical than chloride transport for preventing muco-obstruction in mouse airways.
